clue.text: Back on one's feet when freed of responsibility?

definitions.text: Back on one's feet when freed of responsibility?

parts.words: Back on one's feet when freed of responsibility?
parts.note: someone standing again rather than doing a handstand is literally no longer resting on the palms, which is also the idiom for being relieved of a duty

explanation.surface: Someone recovers and stands tall once a burden is lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a duty or charge that is now somebody else's concern, so you are no longer answerable for it.

clue.text: It's this that gets a person depressed

definitions.text: It's this that gets a person depressed

parts.words: It's this that gets a person depressed
parts.note: read literally, a single individual pushed lower; it is also the crossword label for the first downward clue in a grid

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark about what brings people low.
explanation.definitionFit: In crossword numbering the label names the first clue in the downward list, while literally it is a single individual brought low.

clue.text: Liking to be escorted and handled lovingly

parts.note: fond of means having a liking for
led means guided or escorted

explanation.surface: Someone who enjoys being accompanied and caressed with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress something tenderly is to touch it with affection, the past tense matching the clue's participle.

clue.text: Shift scenery as required

indicators.note: scenery is shifted between acts, and here the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Stagehands move the backdrop when the play demands it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' reads as the stagehands' job but signals rearranging SCENERY and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed or compulsory is essential, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Small group of players displays energy

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a side of players is a team

explanation.surface: A small band of musicians or actors shows plenty of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour or drive is informally called this, as in running out of it or letting it off.

clue.text: He offends in helping a gambling man

parts.note: one who places bets is a better

explanation.surface: A man who backs a gambler is himself doing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a roundabout way of describing an accomplice who aids a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice encourages or assists wrongdoing, sharing in the offence by giving help.

clue.text: Play about the church produced with foreign money

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the play goes around the church abbreviation

parts.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A drama staged around a church is financed from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Greece before the euro was this coin, a foreign denomination to British solvers.

clue.text: The reason for lawfulness is a debatable question

definitions.meaning: read playfully, the purpose of having rules is the aim of being orderly
in meetings, a procedural objection raised for the chair to rule on

explanation.definitionFit: In a formal meeting a member raises a procedural query about the rules, and literally it is the purpose served by keeping things orderly.

clue.text: Concerned with the main abuse of cocaine

indicators.note: abuse means misuse or mistreatment, so the drug's letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A remark about the chief problem of drug misuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic term for the open sea, not the principal thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the sea, so something relating to it belongs to the ocean.

clue.text: Closely observe a sphere in orbit

definitions.meaning: to stare at someone hard and appraisingly
the orbit is the bony socket of the skull, and the globe sitting in it is the organ of sight

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stare at intently; as a noun it is the round organ of sight lodged in the skull's socket.

clue.text: Down in the dumps when short of the hard stuff

definitions.text: when short of the hard stuff
definitions.meaning: running low on liquor such as whisky or gin

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means dejected, and read literally it describes a bar running low on liquor.

clue.text: Farinaceous fare for fools

definitions.meaning: food made from flour, such as long strips of pasta
a noodle is old slang for a simpleton

explanation.definitionFit: These are strips of pasta made from flour, and in old slang a simpleton was called a noodle.

clue.text: He is lacklustre man with wife

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dull fellow is described along with his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a man's given name, borne by one of the Gospel writers.

clue.text: Had made an acknowledgement

definitions.meaning: confessed or admitted, as in owning up

explanation.definitionFit: It means possessed, and also admitted, as in owning up to a mistake.

clue.text: Find out about sectarian differences

indicators.note: differences suggest the letters are made different, rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: An inquiry into disputes between religious factions.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover or establish something for certain is a synonym of learning the facts.

clue.text: Rally competitors find streams of fish (2-7) 172240 pounds can initially ensure an annuity

parts.note: cod is a fish
rivers are streams

explanation.surface: Motor-rally drivers discover fishy rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order in the clue: streams of fish gives fish first then streams.
explanation.definitionFit: In rallying, a navigator shares the car and the driving with the main driver as a partner.

clue.text: Excelled in open-air theatre?

parts.note: read literally, actors performed outside rather than indoors; the idiom means beat an opponent

explanation.surface: Actors shone at an outdoor performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent by playing better is the idiom, while literally the performance happened outdoors.

clue.text: 2240 pounds can initially ensure an annuity

parts.note: an imperial ton is 2240 pounds
a tin is a can

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of the word ensure is taken

explanation.surface: A heavy weight in a container guarantees a regular income.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a scheme where subscribers share an income, the survivors' shares growing as others die, a form of annuity.

clue.text: Small child featured in stories-that's putting it mildly

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so the child goes within the fibs

parts.note: stories can mean lies, as when a child tells stories
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A toddler appears in tales, an understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: This figure of speech is understatement, saying something is not bad when it is good.

clue.text: Organise one's rig-out

definitions.meaning: to arrange or set up an event

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means arrange or set up, and as a noun an outfit, often an odd one.

clue.text: Crooked rogue rings pious pop enthusiast

indicators.note: rings means surrounds, so the jumbled letters encircle the abbreviation
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of rogue are twisted

parts.note: pi is informal shorthand for pious

explanation.surface: A dishonest villain surrounds a devout fan of pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' turns ROGUE into GROUE, which 'rings' around PI.
explanation.definitionFit: A devoted fan who follows a band on tour is a familiar term from the pop world.

clue.text: Young swimmer thanks many a Slav

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
D is the Roman numeral for 500, used for many
a Pole is a Slav

explanation.surface: Grateful words to numerous Eastern Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog's larva is a young creature that swims before growing legs.

clue.text: Little room for a variety of courses

definitions.text: Little room for a variety of courses

parts.words: Little room for a variety of courses
parts.note: a small space set aside for eating meals, where soup, main and pudding are served

explanation.surface: A cramped classroom offering a range of studies.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small dining area, where meals of several courses are eaten.

clue.text: hath not anything to show more fair" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: hath not anything to show more fair" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: hath not anything to show more fair" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: a quotation from Wordsworth's sonnet on Westminster Bridge with its opening word left out for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A line of Romantic poetry praising a view as unmatched.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the line is missing; the sonnet begins with the name of the planet we live on.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line opens with the world itself, saying nowhere on the globe is lovelier than the London dawn.

clue.text: Arranged sequentially

parts.note: placed one after another, each in its proper place

explanation.surface: Things placed one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Items set out in a proper sequence are correctly ranked, a common phrase.

clue.text: Despite being in the duty list I make merry

indicators.note: being in means placed inside, so the single letter sits within the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties

explanation.surface: Someone on the rota insists on partying anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel noisily is to have a boisterous good time.

clue.text: A feat to make capital out of

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a bold deed; as a verb it means take advantage of.

clue.text: Puts out the props and reads the prologue

definitions.meaning: arranges the stage furniture before a play
speaks the introductory passage that establishes the background

explanation.definitionFit: Literally it is arranging the stage before a play, and figuratively it is introducing the background.
